Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB301.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Jiqi of Nanyue. Jiqi Hongchu owns the retained deployment, shouting the lifetime's joy over the groves' men of mettle and ruling it not only today's.

Senses.Explanation: The lifetime's joy of the Chan records: the once-for-all exclamation at the moment a whole life is settled — promised, handed out, policed. Xueyan Zuqin names the hollowing of birth-and-death and the lighting of every mark the one moment that is the lifetime's joy, then bars the door against turning in its light and shadows and losing the eye, Mi'an Xianjie sets the joy at the lion king's one roar on the sand — the wall standing ten-thousand fathoms, one wrong step toppling a thousand places at once — and mourns the ones who sit all their lives in others' words and silence, Zhe'an Jingfan turns the phrase inside out, ruling the sound-followers who split the lands into the pure and the perilous never win the joy and wrong the Great Physician of Long Life, and Shenfeng Xian hands the joy out with the New Year — the nostriled piercing through crown and brain, blessings arriving in season — with no further need for the Heshan drum, the Yunmen board, or the Xinfeng song. Muchen Daomin sets the joy at the year's last night — exhaustion turns, the turning opens, ice withered and snow grown old and spring breaking back all at once, the studying done — while the fellow who farms another's field and plants no rice waits outside the tally, Tianru Weize rules the whole of it ready-made — heaven-wide, earth-level, use it when wanted, effortless — with the one watchword kept only for failure, Dahui Zonggao's monk cries out the joy at last and gets a double hiss and the verse — eyes empty of the cosmos, buddha-choosing and office-choosing both done, the same road and hand in hand but not the same homecoming — and Jiqi Hongchu shouts the joy over the groves' men of mettle and rules it not only today's.
